choices.reason: Condition-novel m128 has a broad current V2 prediction, so this label can calibrate whether broad intervals correspond to real finish tails in a heteroatom-containing aromatic scaffold.
A donor-free high-strength m70 control tests ordinary V1/V2 calibration in a compact hydrophobic ketone family and checks whether polar-scaffold tail corrections transfer to simple rows.
This molecule-novel m45 point adds an acid-like functional-group transfer anchor at ordinary strength, helping distinguish chemical novelty from solvent-regime failure.
The m59 1/1, 150-ul point is a matched loading extension of measured m59 behavior at 1/1, 100 ul in 19bdb9c6c59639662992, directly testing onset and finish sensitivity to loading.
This m153 high-strength point samples a halogenated ether-like scaffold in a moderate loading regime, providing a centered chemical control near the stronger-condition transfer region.
The m168 1/1 point supplies an ordinary anchor for a scaffold with a wide predicted finish interval and can be compared with measured low-strength and high-strength m168 regimes.
A high PE/EA m2 point tests solvent-strength transfer in donor-free dibrominated chemistry, where a global polarity trend may be adequate or may fail through structural packing effects.
This m170 extreme-strength point probes the upper end of a condition curve with a broad predicted V2 response and can identify whether late elution is scaffold-specific.
The matched lower-strength m170 point provides a local baseline for the high-strength experiment, allowing the retrained model to learn the solvent-response slope rather than only an endpoint.
m209 has very broad current V1/V2 predictions at high PE/EA strength. Measuring this polar phenol-like scaffold is a direct information probe for V2-tail calibration in a chemically distinct regime.
Molecule-novel m95 supplies a moderate-strength transfer label with a broad predicted V2 interval, testing whether finish-tail bias persists in compact carbonyl-rich chemistry.

The m109 control adds a donor-free halogenated anisole-like row at moderate strength; together with measured m109 high-strength behavior in 066397bae21d5a7046a6, it tests ordinary solvent-response transfer.
This m105 high-strength PE point expands chemical coverage around donor-containing ester/phenol-like chemistry and tests whether broad V2 corrections transfer outside the major tail families.
Molecule-novel m162 provides a compact nitrile/halogen transfer control at ordinary strength, useful for checking that V1 and V2 repairs do not overcorrect donor-free rows.
The m207 low-strength anchor complements measured m207 1/1 behavior in eb36ddda7c31d7efdac5 and the later high-strength regime, helping locate the onset of its condition response.

This m71 intermediate-strength point tests whether the donor-free scaffold remains compact as strength rises, using measured m71 behavior at 10/1 and 50/1 in e9aa21d2af3158cfa4f5 and 7e981ba02c83f74f5e65 as response anchors.
The m168 1/1, 150-ul point is a loading replicate around the ordinary m168 regime, helping separate sample loading from mobile-phase effects.
This high-strength m155 control extends non-hydrogen-bonding chemistry into a stronger solvent regime and tests whether recent tail repairs preserve calibration for narrow-width rows.
The m136 low-strength donor-free point is a compact control for onset and finish calibration, useful for checking transfer across simple halogenated aromatic chemistry.
The m111 high-strength point adds a condition-response label for a compact anisole/halogen family and tests whether ordinary donor-free rows remain centered across PE/EA.
This m25 moderate-strength carbonyl control tests smooth solvent response in a compact acceptor-rich scaffold and can constrain overcorrection of V2 tails.
The m132 low-loading PE point adds a hydrophobic control at moderate strength, checking whether loading and solvent corrections learned from polar rows generalize to donor-free chemistry.
This m83 ester point samples a moderate PE/EA regime and helps distinguish a smooth ester response from the sharper transitions seen in more strongly interacting scaffolds.
The m159 2/1, 150-ul point fills the local curve between measured m159 1/1 results in d3d2b36ec3417c1c1c6c and cfcf2b8c54d4c8b3838a and the later large tail in a17bcdddcf0799baeee2.
This m88 low-strength point supplies an onset and finish anchor before the measured broad m88 regime represented by d2921349ba8d9cef15a4, testing whether the tail emerges sharply with condition.
The m148 high-strength PE control extends a donor-free aromatic condition curve and provides a centered comparison for whether solvent-strength effects are broadly transferable.
This m150 moderate-strength heavy-halogen control complements measured m150 behavior in 9aaaa2db5c44818c3abd and tests ordinary V2 calibration outside polar tail families.
Molecule-novel m47 provides a chemically distinct nitrile-containing transfer anchor with a comparatively broad predicted finish interval, testing descriptor transfer and V2 calibration together.
The m42 PE point is a compact acetophenone-like control at moderate strength, useful for checking whether recent tail repairs preserve calibration for ordinary carbonyl rows.
This m23 low-strength control broadens coverage to a nonaromatic ester-like scaffold and checks whether the model's solvent and width behavior remains centered outside the selected failure families.
The m88 1/1, 50-ul point is a loading-response control around the low-strength m88 experiment and can distinguish loading-driven width changes from a solvent-driven transition.
This m80 ordinary PE control can be compared with the measured stronger-condition m80 result in 26df752cf7c0673db585, testing smooth solvent-response transfer in a simple diester.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response and onset/finish coupling remain scaffold-specific, with sharp or irregular transitions that a global PE/EA trend does not represent well.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local transition labels can teach scaffold-condition interactions and reduce transfer errors across solvent regimes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do transition locations transfer within functional-group families, or must they be learned locally for each scaffold?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume affect onset and finish differently across scaffolds and solvent regimes; mass alone is insufficient as a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading experiments can separate loading effects from mobile-phase effects and improve V2-tail prediction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA ratio, does loading primarily shift V1, expand V2, or depend on scaffold-specific retention regimes?

hypotheses.content: V2 and interval width require direct local calibration separate from V1 calibration; broad predicted intervals are not reliable uncertainty estimates.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct finish labels can repair tail bias even where onset is reasonably predicted and can teach when broad widths are chemically meaningful.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can descriptors and conditions predict finish-tail width across scaffolds, or are local scaffold-condition anchors necessary?

hypotheses.content: Novelty alone is insufficient; centered controls with distinct functional groups are needed to determine whether transfer gaps arise from chemistry or extreme conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls constrain overcorrection and test whether repairs learned from tail-heavy rows generalize to ordinary chemistry.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: After local V2 repair, do ordinary donor-free and compact carbonyl rows remain centered across PE/EA and loading regimes?

hypotheses.content: Heteroatom-rich or carbonyl-rich scaffolds have narrow condition regions where retention changes sharply; transition-zone labels are more informative than additional extremes alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Boundary labels can identify where QGeoGNN changes from ordinary retention to late, broad elution and improve interpolation across the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do transition locations align across related scaffolds, or are they controlled by local steric and hydrogen-bonding environments?

feedback_interpretation: Recent labels strengthened the case for local condition curves and matched loading experiments, while weakening the use of predicted interval width as generic tail uncertainty. The m118, m159, and m114 intermediate points were informative local anchors, whereas m104 showed that loading corrections are scaffold-specific and m144, m98, m11, m85, and m74 showed that broad predicted widths can overstate measured V2. The batch therefore combines condition-response controls, loading comparisons, direct V2 calibration, molecule-novel transfer points, and ordinary donor-free anchors.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments span condition-novel controls, high-strength and low-strength anchors, matched loading points, molecule-novel transfer chemistry, and compact ordinary rows. m59, m168, m170, m159, and m88 provide local loading or condition comparisons; m209 and m95 probe broad predicted tails; m47 and several donor-free controls test chemical transfer. This balance should improve generalization by teaching both scaffold-specific nonlinear response and the calibration boundaries needed to avoid overcorrecting the broader Row-distribution.
